draft.title: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights
card: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) was adopted by the United Nations (UN) General Assembly in 1948. It was drafted after the Second World War.
It sets out rights that apply to all people, in every country. It is a statement of shared standards, not a treaty.
The UDHR is not legally binding itself. A state that ignores it does not break a treaty obligation by that alone.
It still had a lasting effect. It led to binding treaties, such as the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR), which states choose to join.
draft.remember: The UDHR is a non-binding list of rights for all people that led to binding treaties.

a.q: Which statement about the legal status of the UDHR is correct?
opts: It is not binding itself, but it led to binding treaties
It is a binding treaty that every UN member must obey
It is not binding and has had no effect on later treaties
It became binding only on states that voted for it in 1948
a.why: The UDHR is a declaration, so it is not binding by itself. Later treaties built on it and do bind the states that join them. It is wrong to say it had no effect, because its influence is the reason those treaties exist.
a.clue: Think about what a declaration is compared with a treaty.

b.q: Country X has joined the ICCPR, a treaty based on the UDHR. Country Y has only said it supports the UDHR. Which is the best description of their positions?
opts: Country X has binding treaty duties, but Country Y does not
Both countries have the same binding duties under the UDHR
Country Y has binding duties, but Country X does not
Neither country has duties, because treaties cannot bind states
b.why: Joining a treaty creates legal duties for that state. Supporting the UDHR alone does not, because the UDHR is not binding itself. The two are not equal, since one rests on a treaty and the other on a declaration.
b.clue: Which country has joined something that binds it?
